history.pageHint: Every change to a configuration resource: who made it, when, from where (web, CLI, apply, Terraform, a task) and why. Open a row to compare it and restore it.
history.emptyHint: History starts when the cluster finished its upgrade to this version. Widen the period or clear the filters.
history.emptyResource: No recorded changes to this resource.
history.onlySet: Showing changes made by apply set {{name}}.
history.resourceHint: Changes to this resource, newest first. Open one to compare it or restore it.
history.secretHint: Secrets are not kept in the history: only whether they were set or changed. Restoring keeps the current secret.

restore.title: Restore {{name}} to its values at record #{{revision}}?
restore.recreateTitle: Recreate {{name}} with its values at record #{{revision}}?
restore.hint: The server plans the change; nothing is written until you restore. Secrets, the name and the power state are not restored. Every field goes back to its value then — fields left at their defaults are reset; secrets added since stay.
restore.recreateHint: The resource comes back with the same id, so what pointed at it works again. Its data (disks, backups) is not restored.
restore.nothing: The resource already has those values.
restore.nameTaken: The name {{name}} is used by another resource now. Give a new name to recreate it under (it gets a new id).
restore.changed: The plan changed while you were reading it. Review it again and restore.
restore.stale: The resource changed or the plan expired. Review the new plan and restore again.
restore.force: Take over from Terraform and restore anyway
restore.forceHint: Terraform manages this resource. Restoring it here makes it differ from your Terraform configuration, so the next terraform apply changes it back unless you update the configuration too.

point.open: Restore to a point in time…
point.title: Restore to a point in time
point.hint: Put every resource in the scope back the way it was at that time. Review the server's plan before restoring. Every field goes back to its value then — fields left at their defaults are reset; secrets added since stay.
point.scopeNeeded: Choose a folder, an apply set or a kind.
point.dataLoss: Also delete VMs, volumes and backup stores created since then (their data is lost)

history.intro: Every change to the settings is recorded: who changed it, when, and from where (UI, command line, YAML apply, Terraform, automatic tasks). Open a row to compare before and after and restore an earlier value.

sourceHints.web: A person changed it in the web UI
sourceHints.cli: A person changed it with orbivisorctl
sourceHints.api: A script or another program changed it through the API
sourceHints.apply: Changed by applying YAML files with orbivisorctl apply
sourceHints.task: A running task (migration and so on) changed it
sourceHints.system: The cluster changed it by itself (no one asked)

history.restoreHint: Puts the settings back as they were when this row was recorded. It first shows what will change and applies only when you confirm. Secrets such as passwords, the name and the power state stay as they are.
history.recreateHint: Creates the deleted resource again with the same id. It first shows the plan. Data such as disks and backups is not brought back.
